intro: To calculate the percentage change in Excel on a Mac, use the formula equals open parenthesis new value minus old value close parenthesis divided by old value. This simple calculation allows you to track growth or decline across any dataset in your spreadsheet.
tldr: Enter the formula =(New_Value-Old_Value)/Old_Value into your cell.
Select the resulting cell and press ⌘ + ⇧ + % to format as a percentage.
Ensure your old value is not zero to avoid the #DIV/0! error.
Use IFERROR to handle potential blanks or zero values in your data.

blocks.text: Calculating percentage change is a common task for business analysts and casual users alike. You need two numbers to perform this calculation. The first is your starting point, which we call the old value. The second is your current point, which we call the new value. The difference between these two numbers is then divided by the old value to find the percentage.

Open your Excel workbook on your Mac. Suppose your original value is in cell A2. Your new value is in cell B2. Click on cell C2 to start your calculation. Type the equals sign to tell Excel you are writing a formula. Then type the open parenthesis, click cell B2, type the minus sign, click cell A2, and type the closing parenthesis. Finally, type the division symbol followed by cell A2. Your formula should look like this: =(B2-A2)/A2.

After you press enter, Excel might show a decimal number like 0.25 instead of 25%. This is normal because Excel calculates the raw value first. You can easily change this to a percentage. Select the cell containing your result. Look at the Home tab on your ribbon. Find the Number group. Click the button labeled Percent Style, which shows a percent sign. Alternatively, use the keyboard shortcut ⌘ + ⇧ + % to apply this formatting instantly.

If you need more or fewer decimal places, look for the Increase Decimal or Decrease Decimal buttons in the same Number group on the Home tab. These buttons allow you to control the precision of your percentage display without changing the underlying value of the cell.

One common error is the #DIV/0! error. This happens when your old value is zero. You cannot divide by zero in mathematics or in Excel. If your data contains zeros, use the IFERROR function to handle it. Your formula becomes =IFERROR((B2-A2)/A2, 0). This tells Excel to return a zero if an error occurs instead of showing the error message.

Another frequent mistake is multiplying by 100 manually. Many people write =(B2-A2)/A2*100. This is unnecessary if you use the Percent Style format. Excel does the math for you. If you do both, your results will be off by a factor of 100. For example, a 25% increase would show up as 2500%.

faq.question: Can I use this formula in Excel for the web?
faq.answer: Yes, the percentage change formula works identically in both the desktop version of Excel for Mac and the web-based version.

faq.question: Why does my result show 5000%?
faq.answer: You likely multiplied your result by 100 while also applying the Percent Style format. Remove the *100 from your formula.

faq.question: How do I fix the #DIV/0! error?
faq.answer: This happens if your old value is zero. Use the IFERROR function to wrap your calculation and return a default value like 0.

task: Calculate the percentage change between two values in an Excel cell.
appliesTo: Microsoft Excel for Mac (Microsoft 365 and Excel 2024)
requirements: Two numerical values in adjacent cells

steps.name: Enter the formula
steps.text: Click the cell where you want the result. Type =(New_Value-Old_Value)/Old_Value. Replace New_Value and Old_Value with your cell references.

steps.name: Apply percentage formatting
steps.text: Select the result cell. Press ⌘ + ⇧ + % on your keyboard to format the number as a percentage.

steps.name: Adjust decimal places
steps.text: If you need more precision, click the Increase Decimal button on the Home tab of the ribbon.

troubleshooting.fix: Ensure your old value is not zero. Use IFERROR to handle empty cells.
Remove any manual *100 from your formula if using Percent Style.
